page.layout: One printed page, one text column with narrow marginal notes down the left side. Running head and page number at the top. Catchword at the bottom right. No headings. Show-through from the reverse side on the right and faint marks in the left margin are not transcribed.

main_text.p: Hoc veluti receptaculū pituitæ est, in eoq; colici dolores generantur.
Rectum est intestinum crassum, spinæ recta incumbens, seu à summo osse sacro ad extremum usq; coccygen delatum, atq; ita recto ductu in podicem desinés.
In hoc sunt venæ Hæmorrhoidales, ductæ à vena portæ, & in hoc directæ, per quas sanguis expurgatur Melancholi-cus.
Excrementa porrò tenuia & fluida sunt vel secundæ, vel tertiæ concoctionis.
Excremen-ta secun-dæ concoc-tionis. Vrina.Secundæ concoctionis excrementum est præcipuè serosus humor, qui dicitur Urina.
Urina est excrementum serosum, è sanguine emulctum, in renes secretum, & in vesicam plenius expurgatum.
Urinæ excernendæ membra sunt duorum generum: Primum continet venas emulgentes & renes.
Vena e-mulgen-tes.Venæ emulgentes, sunt vasa è vena cavâ descendentia, quæ quicquid in sanguine est serosum & aqueum emulgent, & in renes devehunt.
Renes.Renes, sunt membra excretioni urinæ inservientia, substantiæ solidæ & compactæ, spinam versus gibba, cava quà viscé-

page.notes: The first word of the page is printed at the top of the text and may continue from the previous page. Faint grey marks in the left margin above "Rectum", and a faint "Colon." beside the Urina passage, look like show-through from the reverse side and are not transcribed; if they are printed notes, they are missing. "serosus" (secundæ paragraph) is read with doubt because the word is partly obscured. "emulctum" uses the ct ligature as printed. The catchword "viscé-" is taken as the hyphenated word that continues onto the next page.
